Service Monitor

Runtime telemetry read over the appliance's REST monitor API — box sessions, per-policy sessions, latency and backend health, throughput and HTTP transactions on FortiWeb; licence headroom and FortiToken pools on FortiAuthenticator — graded against thresholds.

👤 ForOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsmonitoring.view operations.apply appliances.apply
📍 WhereMonitoring → Service Monitor (every ADOM) (URL /monitoring/services/)

What is it?#

Service Monitor answers how much is each service carrying right now? Every probe here is a REST call to the appliance's monitor API — no SSH and no configuration API — so it keeps reporting on a FortiWeb whose configuration API is refusing calls (for example an expired licence).

For a FortiAuthenticator the limiting resource is not bandwidth but entitlement, so this page grades how much of the licence and of the FortiToken pools is consumed.

All probe mechanics (discover, add, mute, charts, statuses, retention) are shared with Deep monitors and described in Probes.

What does it do?#

Kind (Type in the form) Unit Products Source
Concurrent sessions (box) sessions (plus conn/s) FortiWeb system/status.systemresource
Server-policy sessions & latency sessions, app response time, backend health per member FortiWeb policy/policystatus
HTTP throughput Mbps, graded on the peak of a 60-second sample window FortiWeb policy/policytraffic
HTTP transactions transactions in the window FortiWeb system/status.httptransactions
Licence headroom % consumed FortiAuthenticator /api/v1/systeminfo/
FortiToken pool % assigned FortiAuthenticator /api/v1/systeminfo/

When the page has FortiWeb probes it also shows one card per appliance (box CPU/MEM and a table of monitored server policies: Server policy, Sessions, Conn/s, Throughput, Backends). Clicking a policy opens its detail with the Backend pool members table (Server, Pool, Health, Sessions, Server RTT, App resp.). Everything comes from stored samples.

💡Tip

For charts you only need to look at, prefer the store-backed Service drill-down board on Analytics: one collector call covers every policy, whereas a probe reads one policy per call. Keep probes where you need a grade (warn/crit), which only probes produce.

Requirements#

  • See Probes → Requirements.
  • The appliance's REST API reachable from SATOM. Discovery and the policy picker read the live box, not the cache.

Permissions#

🔑Permission

Same as Probes: reading needs the legacy view gate (any read permission, for example monitoring.view); changing or running probes needs the legacy config_write gate, e.g. operations.apply or appliances.apply.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: opening Service Monitor now requires a read permission instead of sign-in alone; discovered and new probes default to a 3-minute interval, and the discovery dialog names both FortiWeb and FortiAuthenticator for REST telemetry.

How to use#

Discover REST telemetry#

  1. Click Discover from device, pick the appliance, keep REST telemetry ticked, click Discover.
  2. On a FortiWeb this creates: box concurrent sessions, the Total HTTP Throughput aggregate, and for every HTTP/HTTPS server policy a sessions probe and a throughput probe. Policies come from the live policystatus call.
  3. On a FortiAuthenticator it creates one Licence headroom probe per licensed resource that has a ceiling, and one FortiToken pool probe per pool that has tokens imported. Their thresholds are left empty so they inherit the product values.

HTTP transactions probes are never discovered. Add them by hand at a slow interval (the endpoint aggregates over hours).

Add a probe by hand#

  1. Add probe → choose the Type → pick the Device.
  2. In Server policy, type or pick the policy (the list fills from the live box). For HTTP throughput you may use Total HTTP Throughput; leave it empty for Concurrent sessions (box). For the FortiAuthenticator kinds, pick the resource from the list.
  3. Set Warn at / Critical at (0 disables a level; empty inherits).
  4. For HTTP transactions set Window (hours).
  5. Save.

Configuration#

Field Kinds Description Required Example
Server policy (target) policy sessions, throughput, transactions, licence, tokens Policy name as reported by policystatus, the aggregate Total HTTP Throughput, or a FortiAuthenticator resource Yes for policy sessions and transactions pol-shop
Warn at / Critical at all Absolute levels in the kind's unit (sessions, Mbps, transactions, % consumed). Critical must be ≥ warning No (inherits) 500 / 1000
Window (hours) HTTP transactions Bucket width chosen by the appliance (1 h → 5-minute buckets, 24 h → 2-hour buckets) No 1

FortiAuthenticator targets:

Kind Target Meaning
Licence headroom users (default), groups, fsso, ssoma licensed users, user groups, FSSO users, SSO mobility agents
FortiToken pool ftm (default), ftk FortiToken Mobile, hardware FortiTokens

How each kind is graded#

  • Concurrent sessions — against the levels; also warn when the log disk or database status is anything other than Available.
  • Server-policy sessions & latency — policy not enabled, all backends down, some backends down, members without health check, and a changed policy shape are binary facts (see Probes); sessions against the levels; app response time against the inherited response-time limit.
  • HTTP throughput — the window peak against the levels.
  • HTTP transactions — total against the levels; a zero count while the policy carries traffic is a fact (default warn).
  • Licence / FortiToken — percent consumed against the levels. A resource without a ceiling, or a pool with nothing imported, is unknown.

Example#

🧪Example — Alert before a FortiAuthenticator runs out of user seats

Discover REST telemetry on fac-01. A Licence headroom probe for users appears with empty thresholds, inheriting 80 % / 95 % from the FortiAuthenticator scope. At 81 % the probe turns warn, the device badge on Device health follows and the alert engine reports it.

Result#

See Probes → Result.

Troubleshooting#

"a HTTP transactions probe needs a server policy name" (or Server-policy sessions)#

These kinds address one policy. Enter the policy name.

"'X' is not a Licence headroom target — pick one of: fsso, groups, ssoma, users"#

Use one of the listed names (the same applies to FortiToken pool: ftk, ftm).

"no transaction buckets returned (unknown policy name?)"#

The appliance returned no data, usually because the policy name is wrong. Check spelling against policystatus.

"0 transactions reported, but the policy is carrying traffic …"#

The per-policy transaction counter reports nothing for a policy without a web protection profile attached. Attach a profile or remove the probe.

"policystatus failed: …" during discovery#

The live box did not answer. Discovery here needs the appliance reachable.

"monitor API discovery is fortiweb/fortiauthenticator-only (device is …)"#

FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer have no REST-telemetry kinds; use Metrics collection for those products.

"the server-policy picker is fortiweb-only"#

The policy picker only works for FortiWeb devices.

Advanced#

Advanced Notes
  • Throughput samples 60 one-second points per run; at the default 3-minute interval that covers 60 s out of 180. The sample payload records this.
  • Every signal on this page is also collected by Metrics collection with one call per device; the probes remain because they grade and keep their own history.
